title: Beylik of Saruhan
capsule: Han (韓) was one of the seven major states competing in the Warring States period (475–221 BC), occupying a fragmented territory in the central Yellow River basin roughly corresponding to southern Shanxi and northern Henan. It was partitioned out of the old Jin state alongside Wei and Zhao in 403 BC when the Zhou king formally recognized the three successor powers — the so-called Partition of Jin. The smallest and most vulnerable of the major powers, Han was repeatedly squeezed by Qin to the west and Wei and Chu on other flanks; its minister Shen Buhai (d. 337 BC) developed early Legalist administrative theory during a brief period of stability. Qin conquered Han in 230 BC, making it the first of the six states destroyed in Qin Shi Huang's unification campaigns.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Han's core territories are reconstructed primarily from Warring States textual sources (Shiji, Zhanguo Ce) with limited archaeological corroboration; the irregular fragmented boundaries typical of this state make precise geometric rendering inherently conjectural.
